argument_summary: The current record does not support an unqualified claim that certification is already policy-compliant. It does support a narrower position: certification can be defended only on a caveated basis if the audit packet records that aggregate readiness passed by 2.0 points, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and rollout is limited to 6% with rollback and monitoring, while also expressly acknowledging that the supply-chain vendor screening segment remains exposed and below target on sanctions-risk explanation. On this record, rollout controls are supporting context for a reversible launch posture, not a substitute for the policy-required handling of the material limitation.
claims_about_business_cost: A caveated treatment preserves the locked certification path without overstating what the evidence proves. It avoids converting supportive rollout evidence into a broader compliance claim that the record does not sustain, and it keeps the governance basis aligned to the actual launch posture: limited, reversible, monitored, and explicitly constrained by a known exposed limitation.
claims_about_policy: The policy predicate is explicit: rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or covered by reviewed and approved risk acceptance. The admissible record does not show either condition. The same policy also requires disclosure of the material limitation for the named launch use case unless it is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Public model-card and AI-risk guidance supports documenting limitations and managing risk through deployment, but that guidance does not erase the disclosure requirement. The defensible policy position is therefore partial support only: certify with an explicit caveat that the exposed limitation must be treated as a disclosed launch condition, rather than representing the current record as clean compliance.
concessions: The admissible record shows the supply-chain vendor screening segment remains exposed in the rollout cohort while below target on sanctions-risk explanation.
The only risk-acceptance artifact is an unapproved draft with a blank approver line and it does not cover the exposed supply-chain vendor screening segment.
There is no admissible evidence here that the required launch-facing disclosure artifact has already been completed or approved.
Rollout percentage, rollback, and monitoring are supportive controls but do not by themselves satisfy the policy condition for an exposed material weakness.
